trackers.product_line: AppLovin's SDK: its own ad network, run by its Axon AI recommendation engine, and MAX, the in-app bidding auction ad networks use to buy app ad space
data_collected: advertising ID, vendor ID and app set ID
IP address, user agent and HTTP request details
device details: make, model, screen, battery, storage, memory, settings, boot time and integrity signals
the app you use it in, with session and install information
country, time zone and language settings
email address, phone number and user ID, if the app's publisher provides them
purchase and install events that advertisers send
trackers.monetization_model: AppLovin earns from advertisers who buy app installs and ads through Axon Ads Manager, run by its Axon AI recommendation engine, and from a percentage of spend through MAX (its 2025 annual report). It uses what the SDK collects, with your activity in other apps, to choose ads, and passes device data to ad buyers in bid requests (its privacy policy and US privacy notice).

data_flows.purpose: Your advertising ID, app set ID, IP address and device details, which AppLovin uses with what you did in other apps to choose ads for you, and keeps for up to two years
data_flows.wording: According to AppLovin's privacy policy, effective 2026-08-06.

consequences.text: San Diego County alleges that AppLovin collected data from children even when their parents had opted out, and let inappropriate ads appear in children's games despite parental controls.
consequences.wording: Alleged in a lawsuit filed by San Diego County on 2026-10-05.

consequences.text: A Dutch privacy foundation alleges that AppLovin's and Adjust's SDKs collect app users' data, build profiles from it and share it through ad auctions, since 2018, without a valid legal basis or the protections children are owed. It seeks damages and an end to the practices.
consequences.wording: Alleged in a collective action by Stichting The Privacy Collective in the Amsterdam District Court; the summons was issued on 2026-05-21.
